<!-- Authorship: Zaher Abou Shakra -->
# Open Data Product Graphs (ODPG) 1.0

## Evidence and authority boundary

ODPG is a storage-neutral portfolio and decision-context graph. Relationships
are claims, not authorization or proof of business value. The implemented CLI
validates the bundled core JSON Schema and the optional draft
`odpg-value-evidence-0.1` profile. Declare profiles only under
`graph.metadata.x-odpg-profiles`. Unsupported profiles fail validation.
The Governed Agent and Observed Lineage profiles are proposals, not implemented
runtime capabilities. Toolkit capability lists below describe architectural
possibilities; do not present them as features of the current Python scripts.

Use `/schema/profiles/assertion-0.1.json` for `x-odpg-assertion` on nodes/edges.
Keep `origin` (`declared`, `observed`, `inferred`) separate from `reviewStatus`
(`pending`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `deferred`). Do not derive either from
confidence. Traversal preserves assertion metadata; `reviewedPaths` means
current, accepted claims with evidence pointers, not authenticated evidence.
Measurements never automatically establish business value or production readiness.
Agent definitions and agent runs are different concepts. Enforce all access
and authorization outside the graph at the MCP/API boundary.
Use `/examples/value-evidence/aviation.yaml` only as a synthetic fixture.
Core `version` must be a string, and resource references use `$ref`, not `ref`.
The development repository targets the v1.0 core; profile contracts remain drafts.

## Profile vocabulary and implementation status

`odpg-value-evidence-0.1` is the implemented draft. Its additional node types are
`ValueHypothesis`, `Outcome`, `MetricDefinition`, `Baseline`, `Target`,
`Measurement`, `Evidence` and `ReviewDecision`. Its additional edge types are
`tests`, `expects`, `measuredBy`, `hasBaseline`, `hasTarget`, `supportedBy` and
`reviews`; it also reuses core relationships. See Adoption and Evidence Profiles
for directed chains; these terms are not new required core fields or core types.
`odpg-governed-agent-0.1` and `odpg-observed-lineage-0.1` are unimplemented
proposals and are rejected if declared for conformance.
`graph.metadata.status` is graph lifecycle, not assertion review status.
`governanceSignals` preserves policy links from unfiltered context paths;
only `reviewedPaths` applies the edge-review filter. Evidence content and reviewer
authority are not authenticated. New graphs should use canonical `alignsWith`;
the shared toolkit retains `alignWith` only as a legacy spelling.

Use this file as AI-agent guidance for reading, generating, validating, repairing, and reasoning over Open Data Product Graphs documents.

## Primary Resources

- Specification: https://opendataproducts.org/odpg-v1.0/
- YAML schema: https://opendataproducts.org/odpg-v1.0/schema/odpg.yaml
- JSON schema: https://opendataproducts.org/odpg-v1.0/schema/odpg.json
- Shared module: /scripts/odpg_toolkit_core.py
- Schema/profile module: /scripts/odpg_profiles.py
- Assertion schema: /schema/profiles/assertion-0.1.json
- Value Evidence overlay: /schema/profiles/value-evidence-0.1.json
- Synthetic profile example and references: /examples/value-evidence/aviation.yaml and /examples/value-evidence/resources.yaml
- Agent objects JSONL: https://opendataproducts.org/odpg-v1.0/graph/objects.jsonl
- GitHub issues: https://github.com/Open-Data-Product-Initiative/odpg-dev/issues

## Execution dependencies

Use Python 3.11, as tested in CI. From the repository root, install
`requirements-dev.txt` (PyYAML, jsonschema with format validation, pytest and
pytest-cov). Runtime use needs only PyYAML and `jsonschema[format]`. Keep both
support modules beside the CLI scripts, with the bundled `schema/` directory
alongside `scripts/`; downloading a CLI file alone is insufficient.
`odpg_profiles.py` is invoked through shared toolkit operations, not executed
directly. Validate graphs with `odpg_validate.py` before visualising them:
the independent explorer generator performs basic checks, not profile
conformance. The summary command reports counts and does not establish validity.

## AI Agent Guidance

- Use `/schema/odpg.yaml` or `/schema/odpg.json` to validate ODPG graph files.
- Use `/graph/objects.jsonl` for retrieval, relationship classification, traversal planning, graph reasoning, validation hints, and lightweight AI-agent tool calls.
- Use ODPG for graph relationships, nodes, edges, traversal, governance propagation, strategic reasoning, and relationship semantics.
- Use ODPC for catalog discovery; do not model discovery catalogs as ODPG graphs unless relationships or traversal are required.
- Use ODPS for full data product metadata; in ODPG, reference data products as `DataProduct` nodes instead of copying full ODPS content.
- Use ODPV when stable vocabulary terms, semantic mappings, or relationship names are needed.
- Use `confidence` values `high`, `medium`, or `low` for edges.
- Use `x-` prefixed extension fields for implementation-specific metadata or declared optional profiles; do not redefine core ODPG semantics.
- Use `graph.nodes` as an array of node objects and `graph.edges` as an array of edge objects.
- Use `$ref` to point to referenced specifications, resources, or artifacts.
- Keep ODPG graph documents lightweight; avoid embedding full external specifications inside graph nodes.

## Core ODPG Shape

An ODPG graph document should include:

- `schema`
- `version`
- `kind`
- `graph`
- `graph.metadata.id`
- `graph.metadata.name`
- `graph.metadata.description`
- `graph.nodes`
- `graph.edges`

The `kind` value should be `Graph`.

## Common Node Types

- `DataProduct`
- `UseCase`
- `BusinessObjective`
- `KPI`
- `Domain`
- `Dataset`
- `API`
- `Policy`
- `Workflow`
- `Agent`
- `Capability`
- `StrategicOpportunity`

## Common Relationship Types

- `uses`
- `supports`
- `contributesTo`
- `measures`
- `tracks`
- `dependsOn`
- `produces`
- `consumes`
- `governedBy`
- `ownedBy`
- `alignsWith`
- `relatedTo`
- `impacts`
- `derivedFrom`
- `exposes`
- `monitors`
- `identifies`

## Tooling Guidance

- Use `/graph/objects.jsonl` as the agent-friendly one-object-per-line resource for graph retrieval and reasoning over ODPG concepts.
- Use the Graph Validation Toolkit for schema, node, edge, reference, semantic consistency, and confidence validation.
- Use the Graph Traversal Toolkit for path discovery, dependency traversal, governance propagation, impact analysis, semantic navigation, and strategic alignment analysis.
- Use the Strategic Intelligence Toolkit for orphan KPI detection, strategic gap analysis, thematic clustering, opportunity inference, duplicate use case detection, and capability alignment analysis.
- Use the AI Agent Toolkit for graph retrieval APIs, semantic context injection, governance-aware traversal, relationship discovery with evidence metadata, explainable reasoning paths, graph-based memory, objective-aware planning, policy-aware execution, dependency reasoning, and graph-native orchestration.
- Federation is an architectural proposal, not an available reference service; do not claim the current scripts implement cross-domain discovery, synchronization or distributed enforcement.

## Generation Rules

- Prefer explicit, typed nodes over ambiguous generic nodes.
- Prefer meaningful edge types over `relatedTo` when a more specific relationship exists.
- Do not invent required fields beyond the official schema.
- Do not copy ODPS data product metadata into ODPG graph nodes; use references.
- Do not use ODPC catalog objects for relationship traversal; use ODPG nodes and edges.
- Preserve existing IDs when repairing a graph unless a duplicate or invalid ID must be fixed.
- Add `x-` fields for local metadata or published optional profiles; keep their contract and declaration explicit.
